feedback: If a learner forces a pupa onto the grasshopper or bird, point back to its real stages: incomplete metamorphosis has no pupa; a bird is egg→chick→adult.
If a learner thinks the plant cycle lacks reproduction, highlight that seed and flower play that role.

Reinforce the shared grammar: both rings close, both use direction arrows ('develops into' between stages, plus a closing arrow showing the adult producing eggs or seeds), even though stage counts differ.
activities.intendedInsight: The same diagram grammar (nodes, directional arrows, closed loop) carries different content: different organisms have different numbers and kinds of stages, which is why you cannot force one template onto every organism.
learnerActions: Build or examine a butterfly ring (4 stages) next to a grasshopper ring (egg→nymph→adult, 3 stages).
Also compare a flowering plant cycle: seed→seedling→mature plant→flower/fruit→seed.
State at least one difference using both diagrams — e.g. 'the butterfly has a pupa/chrysalis stage; the grasshopper doesn't.'
Identify what plays the 'reproduction' role in the plant (seed/flower), since there is no obvious egg.
activities.title: Compare two cycles side by side

feedback: If arrows or labels are left off, scaffold the conventions (label each stage; add direction arrowheads) rather than reteaching the life cycle.
If the line dead-ends at the adult, prompt for the reproduction arrow back to the start.
Check the stage count and names fit the actual organism.
activities.intendedInsight: You own the conventions when you can produce a correct, looped, labelled diagram unaided, with the shape matching the organism's real life cycle.
learnerActions: Given a list of an organism's stages, draw your own labelled cycle on paper from scratch.
Add an arrowhead to every arrow to show direction, and close the loop back to the start.
Choose the correct number of stages for the organism (don't copy the butterfly's four onto a bird or grasshopper).
Label each stage with its proper name.
activities.title: Freehand transfer on paper
